'''Musashi-Mitake Shrine''' (武蔵御嶽神社) is a Shinto shrine located on the summit of {{ill|Mount Mitake (Tokyo)|ja|武蔵御岳山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Mitake (Tokyo)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in {{ill|Ōme, Tokyo|en|Ōme, Tokyo|qid=Q237683|lt=Ōme, Tokyo|1=Ōme, Tokyo}}, {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|qid=Q1490|lt=Tokyo|1=Tokyo}}, formerly within Tama District, {{ill|Musashi Province|en|Musashi Province|qid=Q907398|lt=Musashi Province|1=Musashi Province}}.

"Mitake" refers to {{ill|Mount Kinpu|ja|金峯山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Kinpu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 金峰山|1=Mount Kinpusen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10563986}} in Yoshino, Nara Prefecture, a central site of Shugendo. It enshrines {{ill|Zaō Gongen|ja|蔵王権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zaō Gongen|qq=}} and {{ill|Kushimachi-no-Mikoto|ja|櫛真智命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushimachi-no-Mikoto|1=Kushimachi no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q108039939}}, becoming significant as a mountain worship site since medieval times, with influence in Musashi and Sagami. Some theories identify it as the Shikinai Shrine "Ōmato no Zu Ten Shrine" (see {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Musashi Province|ja|武蔵国の式内社一覧|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Musashi Province|qq=}}). It is currently an independent shrine, not affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|qid=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}.

Due to its enshrinement of {{ill|Ōkuchi Magami|ja|大口真神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuchi Magami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 真神|1=Ōkuchi no Magami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2349235}} (dog deity), it attracts visitors bringing dogs for prayer. The {{ill|Mitake Tozan Railway|en|Mitake Tozan Railway|qid=Q6880754|lt=Mitake Tozan Railway|1=Mitake Tozan Railway}} allows dogs without cages.

== History ==
The shrine is traditionally said to have been established during the 7th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin|1=Emperor Sujin}}'s reign (91 BCE). {{ill|Gyōki|en|Gyōki|qid=Q1136664|lt=Gyōki|1=Gyōki}} is believed to have enshrined {{ill|Zaō Gongen|ja|蔵王権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zaō Gongen|qq=}} here in the 8th year of the Tenpyō era (736 CE).

In the first year of Bunryaku (1234), {{ill|Ōnakatomi no Kunika|ja|大中臣国兼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōnakatomi Kunikane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} restored the shrine from ruin. The shrine became known as a training ground for {{ill|Shugendō|en|Shugendō|qid=Q1483875|lt=Shugendō|1=Shugendō}}, receiving numerous offerings from samurai families. During the Edo period, the shrine underwent major renovations, including a reconstruction of the main hall in 1605 under {{ill|Ōkubo Nagayasu|en|Ōkubo Nagayasu|qid=Q133746|lt=Ōkubo Nagayasu|1=Ōkubo Nagayasu}}.

With the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri|1=Shinbutsu bunri}} policy in the Meiji period, the shrine was renamed from Mitake Daigongen to "Ōmazuto no Mitama Shrine," theorized as the shrine mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}. This name was later changed to "Mitake Shrine" due to other shrines making similar claims. In 1952, it was renamed "Musashi-Mitake Shrine."

== Grounds and structures ==
[[File:武蔵御岳神社_本殿.jpg|thumb|200px|Honden]]
;Main Shrine
:Single-bay Shinmei-zukuri built in 1877. Holds Zaō Gongen statue shown every 12 years. The main hall ({{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|en|Haiden (Shinto)|qid=Q3125745|lt=Haiden|1=Haiden (Shinto)}}) is an elaborate structure with red paint, carvings, and a {{ill|Karahafu|en|Karahafu|qid=Q977293|lt=Karahafu|1=Karahafu}} gable.

;Other shrines on-site:
* Futahashira Shrine (Izanagi, Izanami)
* Yahashira Shrine (Kasuga, Hachiman, etc.)
* Kitano Shrine (Sugawara no Michizane)
* Kofuku Shrine (Haniyasuhime)
* Shinmei Shrine (Amaterasu)
* {{ill|Ōguchi no Magami Shrine|ja|大口真神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōguchi no Magami Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (wolf deity)
* Tokiwakakiwa Shrine (Emperors Sujin, Keikō, Ankan, Seiwa, etc., Tokyo-designated cultural property)
* Sumemimanomikoto Shrine (Ninigi-no-Mikoto)
* Tōshō Shrine (Tokugawa Ieyasu)
* Treasure Hall (holds national treasures like armor)
* Hatakeyama Shigetada Statue
* Okumiya (Yamato Takeru)
* Ubuyasu Shrine (Konohanasakuyahime, etc., fertility shrine)
* Zuishin Gate
* Inari Shrine

== Festivals ==
*New Year's, Setsubun, Spring Festival (March 8), Sunrise Festival (May 7–8), Great Purification (June 30), {{ill|Yabusame|en|Yabusame|qid=Q1886157|lt=Yabusame|1=Yabusame}} Festival (September 29, symbolic ritual without horses), Autumn Festival (November 8).

== Cultural Properties ==
=== National Treasures ===
*{{ill|Aka-ito Odoshi Yoroi|ja|赤糸威鎧|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aka-ito Odoshi Yoroi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Red-thread-laced armor with helmet, donated by Hatakeyama Shigetada, late Heian)
*{{ill|Raden Mirror Saddle|ja|円文螺鈿鏡鞍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raden Mirror Saddle|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Circular-pattern raden saddle set, Kamakura)

=== Important Cultural Properties ===
*{{ill|Murasaki Suso Gō Yoroi|ja|紫裾濃鎧|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Murasaki Suso Gō Yoroi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Purple-gradient armor, mid-Kamakura)
*Gilt-edged tachi sword (Kamakura)
*Black lacquer scabbard tachi sword marked "Hōju"

== Access ==
From {{ill|JR East|ja|JR東日本|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR East|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 東日本旅客鉄道|1=East Japan Railway Company|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q499071}} {{ill|Ōme Line|en|Ōme Line|qid=Q385398|lt=Ōme Line|1=Ōme Line}} Mitake Station → Bus to "Cable Car Base" → {{ill|Mitake Tozan Railway|en|Mitake Tozan Railway|qid=Q6880754|lt=Mitake Tozan Railway|1=Mitake Tozan Railway}} to Mitake-san Station → 25-minute walk. Paid parking available at Takimoto station.
